name: Agent-Memory Integrity Leaderboard
tagline: Recall leaderboards measure whether memory returns the right fact. None measure whether a CORRECTION sticks. This one does.
judge: gpt-4o-mini (neutral, ground-truth-blind — reads each system's own recall surface; nobody is scored on a home-field instrument)
principle: We lead with the cell we TIE, and we publish the cells we don't win. A leaderboard you only ever top is one you built to flatter yourself.

cells.title: Value-obscuring revert
cells.question: The user says “go back to what we had” and names no value. Can the store undo a correction on that unmarked command?
cells.framing: A capability gap, not a tuning gap: only a system with an explicit revert channel can undo a correction on command. Judge-independent — the competitors structurally lack the operation; the judge model only shifts inspeximus's absolute rate.

systems.note: intent router restores the predecessor from the version ledger
no revert operation; the corrected value is retained
no revert operation; bitemporal invalidation fires on named contradictions, not an unnamed “go back”

cells.title: Echo resurrection
cells.question: After a correction, if the OLD value is re-stated, does the store keep the corrected value or resurrect the stale one?
cells.framing: A TIE — all three defend. This is the cell we lead with on purpose.

systems.note: echo_guard blocks the restated stale value
